page.title: Request capacity
page.purpose: Let an operator or tenant ask for a machine, and make the cost and the lifetime consequences clear before they commit.

priorities.statement: What this will cost, before it is requested.
priorities.notes: Including the minimum billable unit, which is the number that surprises people.

priorities.statement: How long it will live, and that it will drain on its own.
Whether there is credit for it, before anything is created.
That a refusal is understandable and says what would fix it.

states.description: The form, with an estimate that updates as the specification changes.
The requested specification is not offered by the selected provider.
The reservation is being taken and the provider is being called.
The instance is creating, with a link to its detail page.
The provider refused or was unreachable, and nothing was created.
The caller may not request capacity.
Provider catalogue and remaining allowance are being fetched, so no estimate can be shown yet.
No provider is configured, so nothing can be requested. The page links to settings rather than showing an unusable form.
The provider catalogue loaded but the remaining allowance did not, so the form is usable and the ceiling is shown as unknown rather than as unlimited.
The cost estimate is based on pricing older than the refresh interval and is labelled as such.

elements.name: Estimated cost
elements.description: Estimated cost for the requested lifetime, with the minimum billable unit and the rounding behaviour stated.

elements.name: Remaining allowance
elements.description: How much of the tenant's ceiling remains, shown before submission.

claims.statement: The estimated cost and the minimum billable unit are visible at the same time as the submit control, without scrolling.
claims.rationale: An estimate the operator has to scroll away from the button to read is an estimate they will not read.

claims.statement: An out-of-credit refusal names which ceiling was reached and what would raise it, and is presented differently from a provider fault.
claims.rationale: The reference metered client collapses out-of-credit and server errors into one path. This page must not inherit that.

claims.statement: A lifetime must be chosen and has no unbounded option.
claims.rationale: Every instance expires. An unbounded machine costs money for as long as nobody notices.

claims.statement: Every declared state renders a distinct, readable surface.
